fields.Summary: BJC | Saga locks | Investigate null-sequence alerts and define recovery (OST-1916)
fields.Description:
Proposed rewrite for existing ticket CEP-3009 ("Inconclusive records report of Saga locks (resulting in false alarm on BJC cloud environment)"). This is not a new issue; it replaces the current CEP-3009 summary and description with the content below. CEP-3009's existing Parent link (CEP-3002) and Assignee are unchanged.

### Summary
Investigate why BJC (environment: customer-production) is generating Datadog alerts for saga length locks with a null sequence id, and define a reviewed recovery procedure support can follow without engineering escalating each occurrence. This rewrite folds OST-1916's new example into the existing open false-alarm ticket for the same BJC symptom rather than opening a second issue.

### Context
CEP-3009 is already open against the same customer and the same shape of problem: BJC saga locks that turn out to be inconclusive or false-alarm records. OST-1916 ("[JOE TO FOLLOW UP CONTENT ASAP] Clearing up Saga Length Locks", Triage, Ready for review, High) reports a new, dated instance of that pattern.

Per OST-1916's Steps to Reproduce field, support was alerted with: "Saga length exceeded its limit in the last 5 minutes. Please log in and start the recovery process for: Customer - 'BJC', Environment - 'customer-production', Server - ''. These locks have 'null' for sequence id. Please provide a script we can run to clear them."

Support reports (comment 159671) that the primary goal is to understand the cause of the saga locks, with resolving them secondary. Support also reports (comment 159681) that one affected patient's record showed two ADT A01 messages "which might have broke the sequencing", with the patient shown as discharged, and (comment 159684) that a null-sequence-id lock located in Mirth had two message mappings differing only by the acknowledgement port, with the patient again shown as discharged correctly.

Two related tickets provide comparison, but neither should be read across to BJC as fact: OST-1524 (NYU) reports locks spiking to approximately 2000, cleared manually by restarting the patient service and clearing the locks, alongside a reported SqlException execution timeout; that count and cause are NYU-specific and not evidenced for BJC. CEP-14390 (SHARP, Done, 2026.R5) landed a data-retention/cleanup remediation and, per comments, a reported feature flag (default false) present since around November 2025 and smoke-tested on OV-STG; whether it applies to BJC's pattern is not established here.

A Confluence search for a dedicated saga-lock SOP returned only Datadog monitor-list pages (for example page 6170705921); no dedicated runbook was found.

### What support observes
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Customer | BJC |
| Sites affected | Environment "customer-production"; location "BJC environment (wide)"; Server field left blank |
| Devices affected | Not known - no device or build information recorded on OST-1916 |
| Symptom | "Saga length exceeded its limit in the last 5 minutes... These locks have 'null' for sequence id." (OST-1916) |
| Frequency | Not established - one confirmed example lock is evidenced; the NYU figure of ~2000 belongs to OST-1524 and does not apply here |
| First reported | Not captured in this evidence pass |
| Current mitigation | Manual recovery via Postman per alert; no clearing script exists today |
| Reproducible off-site | Not established |

### Customer expectation vs actual
Expected: Support expects to be able to run a provided script to clear locks that show a null sequence id, rather than escalating each occurrence to engineering individually (per OST-1916).
Actual: Support currently performs manual recovery per alert; no clearing script exists, and the cause of the null-sequence condition specific to BJC has not been established in this evidence pass.

### Diagnostic gaps
- No confirmed count, rate or device/build detail for BJC's null-sequence locks
- No repeatable, reviewed recovery or clearing procedure exists
- No confirmed reproduction of the BJC null-sequence case outside the customer environment
- No dedicated saga-lock remediation runbook found in Confluence
- No confirmation that the CEP-14390 remediation direction applies to BJC

### Engineering action
The repository and implementation backing the source terminology used in the OST and comments could not be verified against a codebase or repository catalogue in this evidence pass. This ticket is scoped as an investigation and recovery-procedure definition, not a named code change: (1) classify the null-sequence alert records reported for BJC into actionable versus false positive; (2) define and document a repeatable, reviewed recovery procedure, or record explicitly why automation is unsafe; (3) validate against a reproduction scenario in an agreed lower environment, corroborated by BJC monitoring (Datadog) evidence.

### Evidence
OST-1916 description: "BJC | Datadog Alert: [P1] [Triggered] Patient Service || Saga Length Locks". OST-1916 Steps to Reproduce quoted above. OST-1916 comment 159684 (redacted): sequenceId null, messageId <redacted-message-id>, lastProcessedTime 2026-08-13T20:06:42.2619946-05:00. OST-1524 description quoted for NYU comparison only.

### Acceptance criteria
AC-1: A documented classification of the null-sequence alert records reported for BJC exists, distinguishing actionable locks from false-alarm/inconclusive records of the kind CEP-3009 already tracks.
AC-2: A repeatable, reviewed recovery procedure is documented, or, if automation is judged unsafe, that judgement and its reasoning are recorded explicitly instead.
AC-3: The classification from AC-1 gives support a way to tell an actionable lock apart from a false positive going forward.
AC-4: The classification and procedure are validated against a reproduction scenario in an agreed lower environment, corroborated by BJC monitoring (Datadog) evidence.
AC-5: No patient identifiers appear in any log excerpt, comment, or artifact attached to this ticket or its resolution.
This ticket investigates cause and defines recovery; it does not guarantee the underlying saga-length lock condition at BJC is eliminated.

### Out of scope
- A guaranteed root-cause code fix for the saga-length lock condition at BJC
- Applying the CEP-14390 remediation to BJC without separate confirmation
- Sites or customers other than BJC
- Building or shipping an automated clearing script, unless AC-2 concludes automation is safe

### Related
CEP-3009 (subject of this rewrite), CEP-3002 (existing parent, unchanged), OST-1916 (source), OST-1524 (comparison), CEP-14390 (related remediation, Done), CEP-1456 (closest historical symptom match, Done), CEP-1354 (calibration reference, Done), Confluence 6170705921 (monitor list only).

### Known gaps
- Affected devices, models and build versions at BJC
- HubSpot thread references for OST-1916
- Frequency and count of affected BJC locks
- Whether the BJC null-sequence issue reproduces outside the customer site
- Dedicated Confluence runbook for saga-length lock clearing
(Routed to ost-questions.md for support follow-up.)

### Other information
Sites Affected, OST, Device, Impact, Urgency and Affected services are treated as unavailable on the live Defect create screen for this batch and are carried in the body rather than as fields. "Patient Service", "sequence id" and "saga lock" are used only as attributed source terminology from the OST and comments; they were not verified against a codebase in this evidence pass. Patient sequence/message identifiers have been redacted throughout.

---
Suggested estimate: 5 points (M). Investigation-plus-recovery-procedure shape. Calibrated against CEP-14390 (5 points, Done) and CEP-1354 (5 points, Done). Refinement to confirm.
